To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimal configuration of a multiprogramming computer system depends on the workload and the reward structure and that the optimal configuration changes with the workload and reward structure.

(i) a real-time system with an optimal configuration will be reconfigured more often than is commonly believed; (ii) the reconfiguration frequency will be a function of the workload; and (iii) the reconfiguration will be more frequent when the reward structure is changing than when it is constant.

(1) the optimal configuration of a computer system is a function of the reward structure and the workload, (2) the optimal configuration can be computed using a Markov decision process model and (3) a change in the reward structure or the workload should be as powerful an incentive to reconfigure the system as is the failure of one or more components.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of optimally configuring a multiprocessor in real-time environments with periodic workloads and periodic reward structures.
the design of a computer system that is able to reconfigure itself to meet the demands of a changing workload.
the optimal (or quasi-optimal) control of a multiprocessors used in periodic environments.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the configuration of a multiprogrammed computer system should be changed as frequently as necessary to maintain optimal performance, even when the configuration itself is not the cause of the problem.
it should not be assumed that a system should be reconfigured only when a component fails.
